text:
## Observations

1. Every humidifier is a floor cell at distance zero from itself.
2. Each move costs one and leads to an orthogonally adjacent cell inside the grid that is free of walls.
3. A floor cell is humidified exactly when its shortest path from any humidifier has length at most D.
4. A cell reached at distance D counts, and any further move along that path exceeds the limit.
5. The grid contains H × W cells, and each cell has at most four neighbors.

## Solution sketch

> Every humidifier is a floor cell at distance zero from itself.

1. Scan the grid and put every humidifier into one FIFO queue with distance zero. Mark each as visited and include it in the count. This gives the search all its starting points at once. If there are no humidifiers, the queue is empty and the answer is zero.

> Each move costs one and leads to an orthogonally adjacent cell inside the grid that is free of walls.

2. Run breadth-first search from the shared queue. For each dequeued cell whose distance is less than D, examine its four orthogonal neighbors. Skip cells outside the grid and walls. Each remaining neighbor can be reached in one more move.

> A floor cell is humidified exactly when its shortest path from any humidifier has length at most D.

3. The FIFO queue processes cells in order of increasing distance, so the first time a neighbor is discovered gives its shortest distance from any humidifier. For each unvisited neighbor, mark it visited immediately, enqueue it with distance one greater than the current cell’s distance, and increment the count. Marking cells when they enter the queue prevents double-counting when several paths reach the same cell.

> A cell reached at distance D counts, and any further move along that path exceeds the limit.

4. Skip expansion whenever a dequeued cell is at distance D. It has already been counted, and the queue still processes every other cell within the limit. When D is zero, only the humidifiers count. Print the final count after the queue empties.

> The grid contains H × W cells, and each cell has at most four neighbors.

5. The initial scan takes O(H × W) time. Each cell enters the queue at most once and requires at most four neighbor checks, so the total time is O(H × W). The grid, visited marks, and queue use O(H × W) space.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
